mainTopic: The reward for avoiding sin, whether מלקות removes כרת, things Heaven agreed to, רוח הקודש in three courts, and the 613 מצוות
overview: The amud opens with the last lines of the final משנה in מכות. A person who simply holds back from sin is rewarded like someone who does a מצוה. רבי שמעון בר רבי adds a קל וחומר: if staying away from blood earns a reward, staying away from גזל and עריות earns reward for all generations. רבי חנניא בן עקשיא teaches that ה׳ gave many מצוות to give Israel merit. The גמרא then asks whether the חכמים disagree with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל that מלקות removes כרת. A proof from the משנה about שבת and יום הכיפורים is pushed away in two ways, and רב rules like רבי חנניה בן גמליאל. When רב יוסף asks how anyone can know what Heaven does, אביי answers that we learn it from פסוקים, just as with the three things the earthly court did and Heaven agreed to: reading the מגילה, greeting with ה׳'s name, and bringing מעשר. רבי אלעזר then lists three courts where רוח הקודש appeared, those of שם, שמואל and שלמה, but רבא shows the פסוקים do not prove it, so it is known from tradition. Finally רבי שמלאי teaches that משה received 613 מצוות, and רב המנונא begins a גימטריא proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Holding back from sin earns a reward
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי שמעון's teaching in the משנה: from the פסוק 'which a person shall do and live by them,' we learn that someone who simply does not sin gets a reward like someone who does a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Which a person shall do and live by them.' This teaches that a person who just sits and does not commit a sin is given a reward like someone who does a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of the משנה, at the end of רבי שמעון's teaching. He quotes a פסוק and learns from it that not sinning is itself rewarded like doing a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק promises life to a person who 'does' the מצוות. רבי שמעון reads this to include someone who 'does' a לא תעשה simply by holding back from it. So passively avoiding a sin counts as a real, rewarded act.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and live by them' — the reward of life for keeping the מצוות
one who sits, meaning he simply does nothing wrong

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of a new teaching. These are the closing words of רבי שמעון's statement, which began earlier in the משנה.

phrases.english: 'Which a person shall do and live by them.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:5

phrases.english: This teaches that one who sits and did not commit a sin
is given a reward like one who performs a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אשר יעשה אותם האדם וחי בהם הא היושב ולא עבר עבירה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי שמעון's teaching from earlier in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who holds back from sin receives a reward like someone who performs a מצוה.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from blood to robbery and forbidden relations
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בר רבי reasons that if someone is rewarded for avoiding blood, which people find disgusting anyway, then someone who avoids גזל and עריות, which people crave, will certainly be rewarded for all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בר רבי says: The Torah says, 'Only be strong not to eat the blood, for the blood is the soul.' Now, a person finds blood disgusting, and still whoever stays away from it gets a reward. Robbery and forbidden relations are things a person craves. So whoever stays away from them will surely earn merit for himself, his children, and his descendants until the end of all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא adds to the theme of reward for not sinning. He uses a קל וחומר: the harder a sin is to resist, the bigger the reward for resisting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'light' case is blood: people naturally dislike it, yet the Torah still promises a reward for avoiding it. The 'heavy' case is גזל and עריות, which pull strongly at a person. If the easy restraint is rewarded, the hard restraint deserves far more, and the reward reaches all future generations.

keyTerms.meaning: reasoning from a lighter case to a heavier one ('all the more so')
'how much more so' — the wording that signals a קל וחומר
one who keeps away or holds back

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that the reward for keeping away from sin grows with how hard it is to resist.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi, says:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' here means רבי יהודה הנשיא, so this is his son.

phrases.english: Behold, it says:
'Only be strong not to eat the blood,
phrases.notes: דברים 12:23. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: for the blood is the soul, etc.'
Now if blood,
which a person's soul is disgusted by —
one who keeps away from it receives a reward,
then robbery and forbidden relations,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנַּפְשׁוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מִתְאַוָּה לָהֶן וּמְחַמַּדְתָּן –
phrases.english: which a person's soul craves and desires —

phrases.aramaic: הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מֵהֶן עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה
phrases.english: one who keeps away from them, how much more so
will he earn merit for himself and for his generations

phrases.aramaic: וּלְדוֹרוֹת דּוֹרוֹתָיו עַד סוֹף כׇּל הַדּוֹרוֹת.
phrases.english: and for the generations of his generations, until the end of all generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי שמעון בר רבי אומר הרי הוא אומר רק חזק לבלתי אכל את הדם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 1's idea of reward for not sinning and adds a קל וחומר showing how great that reward can be.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoiding sins a person desires, like גזל and עריות, earns merit for oneself and for all future generations.

steps.title: ה׳ gave many מצוות to give Israel merit
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא בן עקשיא teaches that ה׳ gave Israel a great deal of Torah and מצוות because He wanted them to earn merit, as the פסוק in ישעיהו says.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניא בן עקשיא says: The Holy One, Blessed be He, wanted to give Israel merit. That is why He gave them so much Torah and so many מצוות, as it says: 'ה׳ desired, for the sake of His righteousness, to make the Torah great and glorious.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing teaching of the משנה. It explains why there are so many מצוות: each one is another chance to earn merit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The many מצוות are not meant as a burden. They are a gift, giving many chances for reward. The פסוק's words 'make the Torah great' are understood as giving more Torah and מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'to make the Torah great and glorious'

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends on a positive note: holding back from sin is rewarded, and the large number of מצוות is ה׳'s way of giving Israel more merit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya ben Akashya says:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, wanted
to give merit to Israel;
therefore He gave them much Torah and many מצוות,
as it is said:
'ה׳ desired, for the sake of His righteousness,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 42:21

phrases.english: to make the Torah great and glorious.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי חנניא בן עקשיא אומר רצה הקדוש ברוך הוא לזכות את ישראל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A separate closing teaching on the same theme of merit and reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ gave many מצוות in order to increase Israel's merit.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the other חכמים disagree with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins. רבי יוחנן says that רבי חנניה בן גמליאל's colleagues disagree with his view in the משנה that receiving מלקות removes a person's כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יוחנן said: His colleagues disagree with him — with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier part of the משנה, where רבי חנניה בן גמליאל said that people liable for כרת who receive מלקות are freed from their כרת. רבי יוחנן says the other חכמים do not agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן tells us that רבי חנניה בן גמליאל's view is not accepted by everyone. According to his colleagues, מלקות does not wipe away כרת. This sets up the next step, where a proof will be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: the discussion and analysis of the משנה
his colleagues, the other חכמים of his time
lashes given by a בית דין

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the names! רבי חנניה בן גמליאל, who is being discussed here, is a different person from רבי חנניא בן עקשיא in the last step.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Yochanan said:
His colleagues disagree with him
— with Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel.
phrases.notes: Earlier in the משנה, he said that those liable for כרת who get מלקות are freed from their כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יוחנן חלוקין עליו חבריו על רבי חנניה בן גמליאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by going back to an earlier statement in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים disagree with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל and hold that מלקות does not remove כרת.

steps.title: Proof from the difference between שבת and יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה brings a proof from a משנה: the only difference between שבת and יום הכיפורים is that breaking שבת on purpose is punished by people, and breaking יום הכיפורים on purpose is punished with כרת. If מלקות removed כרת, both would be punished by people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: In the house of רב they say: We learned in a משנה: 'The only difference between שבת and יום הכיפורים is that this one, if broken on purpose, is punished by human hands, and that one, if broken on purpose, is punished with כרת.' And if רבי חנניה בן גמליאל were right, both this one and that one would be punished by human hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה supports רבי יוחנן with a proof from a משנה in מגילה. That משנה shows that the תנא there disagrees with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking שבת on purpose (with witnesses and a warning) brings סקילה by a בית דין. Breaking יום הכיפורים on purpose brings כרת. But if רבי חנניה בן גמליאל were right, a בית דין would give מלקות for יום הכיפורים, removing the כרת, so that too would be 'by human hands.' Since the משנה still calls this a real difference, its תנא must hold that מלקות does not remove כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: by human hands — a punishment carried out by a בית דין
both this one and that one

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה in מגילה treats יום הכיפורים as a 'כרת' case and not a 'human court' case. This shows its תנא holds that מלקות does not remove כרת, against רבי חנניה בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
They say in the house of Rav:
We learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מגילה 7b.

phrases.english: The only difference between Shabbat and Yom Kippur
is that this one, its deliberate violation is punished by human hands,
and that one, its deliberate violation is punished with karet.
And if it were so,
phrases.notes: He means: if רבי חנניה בן גמליאל were right that מלקות removes כרת.

phrases.english: both this and that are by human hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמרי בי רב תנינן אין בין שבת ליום הכיפורים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's claim from step 4 with a proof from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the חכמים disagree with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מגילה 7b, which says the only difference between שבת and יום הכיפורים is punishment by people versus כרת

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יצחק, who holds there is no מלקות for כרת sins
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the proof. The משנה about שבת and יום הכיפורים follows רבי יצחק, who holds that a כרת sin gets no מלקות at all. So the משנה says nothing about whether מלקות removes כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק says: Whose view is this משנה? It is רבי יצחק's, who says there is no מלקות for sins that carry כרת. As it is taught: רבי יצחק says, all the כרת sins were already included in one general פסוק. So why was כרת for one's sister mentioned separately? To teach that such a person is judged with כרת and not with מלקות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק pushes back on רב אדא בר אהבה's proof from Step 5. He says that משנה follows רבי יצחק, who holds that כרת sins never get מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא's proof assumed that a person who breaks יום הכיפורים on purpose could get מלקות, so the משנה should have said he is also punished by people. But according to רבי יצחק, יום הכיפורים, a כרת sin, gets no מלקות at all, so כרת is its only punishment. That means the משנה cannot tell us anything about whether מלקות removes כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? A way of tying a source to one particular תנא
Sins that carry the punishment of כרת
They were already included in the general rule
Was taken out (singled out) of the general rule to teach something new

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יצחק is not saying מלקות removes כרת. He is saying מלקות does not apply to כרת sins at all. So the question in this sugya never even comes up for him.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak says:
Whose view is this Mishnah? It is Rabbi Yitzchak's,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה from the previous step about שבת and יום הכיפורים.

phrases.english: who says: there are no lashes for those liable to karet.
As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yitzchak says:
All those liable to karet were included in the general rule,
phrases.notes: The general rule is ויקרא 18:29, which gives כרת for all the forbidden relationships.

phrases.english: so why was karet for one's sister singled out?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:17

phrases.english: To judge him with karet and not with lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אדא בר אהבה's proof by tying the משנה to רבי יצחק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה is rejected. רבי יוחנן's claim could still be true.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed יום הכיפורים could get מלקות. According to רבי יצחק it cannot, so the משנה is silent on whether מלקות removes כרת.

steps.title: Even the Rabbis can explain the משנה: it describes each day's main punishment
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that even according to the רבנן, who do give מלקות for כרת sins, the משנה proves nothing. It is only describing the main punishment of each day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even if you say the משנה follows the רבנן, here is the point: for this one (שבת), the main punishment for doing it on purpose is by people, and for that one (יום הכיפורים), the main punishment for doing it on purpose is by Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second way to push back on רב אדא's proof. This one works even for the רבנן who disagree with רבי יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not listing every possible punishment. It only names the main, built-in punishment of each day: for שבת it is the punishment given by בית דין, and for יום הכיפורים it is כרת. A person might still get מלקות for יום הכיפורים and become free of כרת, and the משנה would still be correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say it follows the רבנן. This shows the answer works even by the other opinion.
The main punishment for doing it on purpose
By human hands, meaning a punishment given by בית דין
By the hand of Heaven, such as כרת

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers protect the משנה from רב אדא's proof. רב נחמן בר יצחק says it follows רבי יצחק, so there are no מלקות for כרת sins at all. רב אשי says that even by the רבנן, the משנה only lists each day's main punishment.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Even if you say it follows the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: The רבנן are the ones who argue on רבי יצחק and do give מלקות for כרת sins.

phrases.english: for this one, its main punishment for doing it on purpose is by human hands,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is שבת.

phrases.english: and for that one, its main punishment for doing it on purpose is by the hand of Heaven.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is יום הכיפורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer that works even without following רבי יצחק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה according to every opinion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof read the משנה as a full list of punishments. It actually names only each day's main punishment.

steps.title: רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי חנניא בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה, quoting רב, rules that the הלכה follows רבי חנניא בן גמליאל: מלקות removes כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי חנניא בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא brings a practical ruling. The הלכה is that receiving מלקות removes a person's כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the proof against רבי חנניא בן גמליאל was pushed away, רב rules like him. This ruling sets up the next step, where רב יוסף questions how such a ruling is even possible.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling: a person who received מלקות from בית דין is free of כרת.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said in the name of Rav:
The halacha follows Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof against רבי חנניא בן גמליאל is pushed away, a ruling is given in his favor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלקות removes כרת, following רבי חנניא בן גמליאל.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks: who went up to Heaven to find out?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges the ruling. כרת is a punishment from Heaven, so how can anyone on earth know that Heaven cancels it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Who went up on high, came back, and told us?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the ruling from Step 8. He asks how an earthly ruling can decide what Heaven does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כרת is given by Heaven, not by בית דין. Saying that מלקות cancels it is a claim about how Heaven acts. רב יוסף asks how anyone could know that without someone having gone up to Heaven to check.

keyTerms.meaning: Who went up on high? A way of saying no one can know what Heaven decides

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Who went up on high, came back, and told us?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just given.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that מלקות removes כרת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only Heaven decides about כרת, so no earthly authority can know that it has been cancelled.

steps.title: אביי answers: we learn it from verses, just like the three things Heaven agreed to
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the same question could be asked about רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching. There, too, we know because we learn it from פסוקים, and the same is true here.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, what about רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching that the earthly court did three things and the heavenly court agreed with them? Who went up on high, came back, and told him? Rather, we learn it from verses. Here too, we learn it from verses.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב יוסף's challenge by comparing it to another accepted teaching. In both cases we know what Heaven does because we learn it from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one has to go up to Heaven. The Torah itself tells us what Heaven does, and we find it by learning the פסוקים. רבי חנניא בן גמליאל's view comes from a פסוק too (the משנה's 'your brother is degraded'), so it can be trusted the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Agreed with them, supported what they did
We learn it by expounding פסוקים

steps.whatToRemember: We know what Heaven does because we learn it from the Torah's פסוקים, not because someone went up to check.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: But then, what about what Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים עָשׂוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַטָּה
phrases.english: Three things the earthly court did

phrases.aramaic: וְהִסְכִּימוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַעְלָה עַל יָדָם –
phrases.english: and the heavenly court agreed with them —
who went up on high, came back, and told him?
Rather, we learn it from verses,
so here too, we learn it from verses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to an accepted teaching, plus naming the source of the knowledge (the פסוקים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Knowing what Heaven does would need someone to go up to Heaven.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוקים themselves tell us what Heaven does, so a ruling based on them is trustworthy.

steps.title: The three things the earthly court did and Heaven agreed to
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching on its own. The three things are reading the מגילה, greeting with ה׳'s name, and bringing מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the teaching itself. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Three things the earthly court did, and the heavenly court agreed with them. They are: reading the מגילה, greeting someone with ה׳'s name, and bringing the מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now studies the teaching that אביי just mentioned and lists the three things. This sets up the next part, where the גמרא will show the פסוק behind each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי only mentioned this teaching in passing, so the גמרא now quotes it fully. The list is the starting point. The proofs from the פסוקים, which show that Heaven agreed, come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Returning to the teaching itself, after it was quoted in passing
Greeting another person using ה׳'s name

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Now to the teaching itself: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים עָשׂוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַטָּה
phrases.english: Three things the earthly court did

phrases.aramaic: וְהִסְכִּימוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַעְלָה עַל יָדָם, [אֵלּוּ הֵן]:
phrases.english: and the heavenly court agreed with them, [and these are they]:
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets; they come from the corrected wording.

phrases.english: reading the Megillah,
and greeting [with ה׳'s name], and bringing the tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes in full the teaching that אביי mentioned in passing, opening a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven agreed with three things the earthly בית דין did: reading the מגילה, greeting with ה׳'s name, and bringing מעשר.

steps.title: The source for reading the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'קיימו וקבלו' shows that Heaven confirmed what the Jews accepted on earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reading the מגילה: as it is written, 'The Jews confirmed and accepted.' This means they confirmed above what they accepted below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the first of the three things, which is reading the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two words, 'confirmed' and 'accepted.' The גמרא reads them as two levels. The Jews accepted the מגילה down here, and Heaven confirmed it up above.

phrases.english: Reading the מגילה –
as it is written: "The Jews confirmed and accepted" –
phrases.notes: אסתר 9:27

phrases.english: They confirmed above
what they accepted below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק for the first item in the list from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That Heaven agreed to the reading of the מגילה

steps.title: The source for greeting with ה׳'s name
steps.stepSummary: בעז greeted the harvesters with ה׳'s name, and an angel greeted גדעון the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Greeting: as it is written, 'And behold, בעז came from בית לחם and said to the harvesters: ה׳ is with you.' And it also says: 'ה׳ is with you, mighty man of valor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two פסוקים as the source for greeting someone with ה׳'s name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows a person, בעז, using ה׳'s name in a greeting. The second פסוק shows an angel doing it. The גמרא will explain next why the second one is needed.

phrases.english: And greeting –
as it is written: "And behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem
phrases.notes: רות 2:4

phrases.english: and said to the harvesters: ה׳ is with you,"
and it says: "ה׳ is with you, mighty man of valor."
phrases.notes: שופטים 6:12. This is the angel speaking to גדעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second item in the list.
steps.raayaObject: That Heaven agreed to greeting with ה׳'s name

steps.title: Why a second פסוק is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it added 'and it says' with a second פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does it say 'and it says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the פסוק about בעז was not enough. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually one פסוק is enough for a proof. Adding a second one with 'and it says' suggests the first proof has a weak point. The גמרא wants to know what that weak point is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it says': brings an extra פסוק

phrases.english: What is the reason for "and it says"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the proof in step 13 needs two פסוקים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the first פסוק about בעז was not enough

steps.title: Maybe בעז acted on his own
steps.stepSummary: From בעז alone, we might think Heaven did not agree. The angel's greeting shows that Heaven did agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you would say that בעז did this on his own and Heaven did not agree with him, come and hear: it also says, 'ה׳ is with you, mighty man of valor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second פסוק shows Heaven agreed, not just בעז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point is that Heaven agreed to what people did on earth. בעז is a person, so his greeting might have been only his own idea. When an angel from Heaven uses the same greeting, it shows that Heaven approved.

keyTerms.meaning: On his own (by his own decision)

phrases.english: And if you would say it was Boaz
who did it on his own,
and from Heaven they did not agree with him –
come and hear: and it says:
"ה׳ is with you, mighty man of valor."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא בּוֹעַז הוּא דַּעֲבַד מִדַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק about בעז only shows a person doing it. The angel's words show that Heaven agreed.
steps.whatToRemember: Each of the three proofs needs to show Heaven's agreement, not only what people did.

steps.title: The source for bringing מעשר
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ tells the people in מלאכי to bring all the מעשר and promises a great blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bringing מעשר: as it is written, 'Bring all the tithe into the storehouse, so there may be food in My house, and test Me now with this, says ה׳ of hosts, if I will not open for you the windows of heaven and pour out for you blessing until there is no "enough."'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the third thing, which is bringing מעשר to the storehouse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here ה׳ Himself asks for the מעשר to be brought to the storehouse. He even promises a blessing for it. This shows that Heaven agreed to this practice.

phrases.english: Bringing the tithe –
as it is written: "Bring all the tithe
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:10

phrases.english: into the storehouse,
so there may be food in My house,
and test Me now with this,
says ה׳ of hosts,
if I will not open for you
the windows of heaven
and pour out for you blessing
until there is no 'enough.'"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the third and last item in the list.
steps.raayaObject: That Heaven agreed to bringing מעשר to the storehouse

steps.title: What does 'עד בלי די' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the unusual phrase at the end of the פסוק means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'until there is no enough' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the meaning of the last words of the פסוק. This sets up רמי בר רב's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'עד בלי די' is unclear. It clearly describes a huge blessing, but its exact wording is unusual, so the גמרא asks what it means.

phrases.english: What does "until there is no 'enough'" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the פסוק in step 16.

steps.title: Your lips will wear out from saying 'enough'
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר רב explains that the blessing will be so great that people will be tired of saying 'enough.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר רב said: Until your lips wear out from saying 'Enough!'
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר רב explains the phrase as a picture of a huge, overflowing blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'בלי' as connected to 'יבלו,' meaning to wear out. So the blessing will be so large that your lips will wear out from saying 'די,' which means 'enough.'

phrases.english: Rami bar Rav said:
Until your lips wear out
phrases.notes: He hears the word בלי in the פסוק as יבלו, 'wear out.'

phrases.english: from saying "Enough."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר רַב עַד שֶׁיִּבְלוּ שִׂפְתוֹתֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עד בלי די' means until your lips wear out from saying 'enough.'
steps.whatToRemember: All three things from רבי יהושע בן לוי now have a פסוק: מגילה, greeting, and מעשר.

steps.title: Three courts where רוח הקודש appeared
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר lists three courts where רוח הקודש openly appeared: the courts of שם, שמואל הרמתי, and שלמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: In three places רוח הקודש appeared: in the court of שם, in the court of שמואל הרמתי, and in the court of שלמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אלעזר with a similar theme: Heaven showing agreement with what happened on earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the list of רבי יהושע בן לוי, this is a list of three. Here, though, Heaven's involvement was openly shown through רוח הקודש. The גמרא will now go through the three courts one by one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
In three places the Divine Spirit appeared:
in the court of Shem,
and in the court of Samuel the Ramathite,
and in the court of Solomon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת הוֹפִיעַ רוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new, similar teaching after the three proofs are done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רוח הקודש openly appeared in the courts of שם, שמואל הרמתי, and שלמה.

steps.title: The court of שם: יהודה admits to תמר
steps.stepSummary: The proof for the court of שם is יהודה's admission, 'צדקה ממני.'
steps.simpleTranslation: In the court of שם: as it is written, 'And יהודה recognized them and said: She is more righteous than I.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts with the first court, the court of שם, and brings the פסוק from the story of יהודה and תמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהודה recognized his own items, which תמר had kept. He admitted that he was the father. The גמרא will now ask how he could be so sure.

keyTerms.meaning: She is more righteous than I (can also be read 'from Me')

phrases.english: In the court of Shem –
as it is written: "And Judah recognized
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:26

phrases.english: and said: She is more righteous than I."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the first court in רבי אלעזר's list.
steps.raayaObject: That רוח הקודש appeared in the court of שם

steps.title: How could יהודה know he was the father?
steps.stepSummary: Maybe another man also went to תמר, so יהודה could not be sure the child was his.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did he know? Perhaps, just as he went to her, another man also went to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges יהודה's certainty that the child was his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that he had been with her does not prove that he was the father. Someone else might have been with her too. So the plain story does not explain how יהודה could be sure.

phrases.english: How did he know?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא כִּי הֵיכִי דַּאֲזַל אִיהוּ לְגַבַּהּ
phrases.english: Perhaps just as he went to her
another person also went [to her]!
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the פסוק brought in step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being with her does not prove he was the father, since another man could also have been with her.

steps.title: A בת קול said: 'From Me'
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול announced that these hidden events came from ה׳. That is the רוח הקודש in the court of שם.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בת קול came out and said: 'From Me these secrets came out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that יהודה did not have to figure it out himself. A heavenly voice confirmed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ממני' is read as ה׳ speaking: 'from Me.' ה׳ announced that these hidden events were His plan. This is how the matter was known, and it is the appearance of רוח הקודש in the court of שם.
steps.confusionAlert: 'ממני' here is not only יהודה saying 'than me.' The גמרא reads the same word as ה׳'s voice saying 'from Me.'

phrases.english: A Divine Voice came out and said:
From Me the secrets came out.
phrases.notes: This is the same word ממני from the פסוק, now read as ה׳ speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק: the word 'ממני' is spoken by a בת קול
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יהודה could not have known for sure that he was the father.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בת קול confirmed it, and this was רוח הקודש appearing in the court of שם.

steps.title: The proof for the court of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוקים where שמואל asks the people to testify that he never took anything from anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the court of שמואל, as it says: 'Here I am, testify against me before ה׳ and His anointed: whose ox have I taken... And they said: You did not cheat us or oppress us... And he said: ה׳ is witness and His anointed is witness... that you found nothing in my hand. And he said: Witness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second court on רבי אלעזר's list, the court of שמואל, and quotes the פסוקים it will use as proof. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל asks the nation to say whether he ever took anything unfairly. The people answer that he did not. At the end of the conversation the פסוק says 'וַיֹּאמֶר עֵד', 'and he said: witness'. That last phrase is what the גמרא will focus on.

keyTerms.meaning: Court. Here it means the court or leadership of a great leader.
His anointed one. Here it means שָׁאוּל the king.

phrases.english: In the court of Shmuel:
as it is written: "Here I am; testify against me
phrases.notes: שמואל א 12:3–5

phrases.english: before ה׳ and before His anointed
whose ox have I taken...?
And they said: You have not cheated us and not oppressed us...
And he said: ה׳ is witness and His anointed is witness...
that you have not found anything in my hand
And he said: Witness."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the court of שם to the second court on רבי אלעזר's list.
steps.raayaObject: That רוח הקודש openly appeared in the court of שמואל

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'he said' and not 'they said'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the answer should be in the plural, because the people are the ones answering.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he said'? It should have said 'And they said'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a strange word in the פסוק. The people are answering שמואל, so it should say 'they said', not 'he said'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole nation is the one confirming שמואל's honesty, so the plural is expected. The singular word suggests that someone else is speaking. This question opens the door to the answer that it was ה׳.

phrases.english: "And he said"?
It should have said "And they said"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the singular wording at the end of the פסוק quoted in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The singular word 'וַיֹּאמֶר' in שמואל א 12:5
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The people are the ones answering, so the פסוק should use the plural.

steps.title: A heavenly voice said 'I am witness'
steps.stepSummary: The singular speaker was a בת קול, which declared that ה׳ is witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said: I am witness in this matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'he' who spoke was not the people. It was a בת קול saying that ה׳ Himself is witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The singular word now makes sense, because one voice was speaking. This is the open appearance of רוח הקודש in the court of שמואל.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said:
I am witness in this matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצָאת בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה אֲנִי עֵד בְּדָבָר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the singular word.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets who is speaking in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'and he said' is the people's answer, which would make the singular wording strange.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בת קול spoke in the singular. ה׳ testified, which shows רוח הקודש in שמואל's court.

steps.title: The proof for the court of שלמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes שלמה's ruling in the case of the two women: give the living child to her, she is his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the court of שלמה, as it says: 'The king answered and said: Give her the living child and do not kill him, she is his mother.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the third court on the list, שלמה's, and quotes his famous ruling about the baby. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two women each claimed the living baby, and שלמה ruled that the woman who wanted to spare the child was the mother. The ending words 'היא אמו', 'she is his mother', are the key words the גמרא will discuss.

phrases.english: In the court of Shlomo:
as it is written: "And the king answered and said:
phrases.notes: מלכים א 3:27

phrases.english: Give her the living child
and do not kill him
she is his mother."
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The פסוק itself just says 'she is his mother'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the court of שמואל to the third court on the list.
steps.raayaObject: That רוח הקודש openly appeared in the court of שלמה

steps.title: How could שלמה be sure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שלמה knew. Perhaps that woman was acting with a trick.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did he know? Maybe she was being sneaky!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how שלמה could be certain. The woman's show of mercy could have been a trick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה's test only shows which woman acted kindly. It does not prove for sure who gave birth. So something more than a clever test must have made him certain.

keyTerms.meaning: She was being crafty, acting with a trick

phrases.english: How did he know?
Maybe she was being crafty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how certain שלמה's ruling in Step 26 really was.
steps.kashyaTarget: שלמה's certainty that 'she is his mother'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The woman's reaction could have been a trick, so the test alone cannot give certainty.

steps.title: A heavenly voice said 'She is his mother'
steps.stepSummary: The words 'she is his mother' were said by a בת קול, not by שלמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said: 'She is his mother.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the final words of the פסוק were said by a בת קול, which confirmed the truth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה said 'give her the living child'. Heaven added 'she is his mother'. That is how the ruling became certain, and it is the open appearance of רוח הקודש in שלמה's court.
steps.whatToRemember: In all three courts (שם, שמואל, שלמה), the גמרא points to something in the פסוק that seems hard to explain and answers that a בת קול spoke.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said:
"She is his mother."

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצָאת בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה הִיא אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how שלמה could be certain.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns who said the words of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלמה said 'she is his mother' based only on his test, which could be wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בת קול said 'she is his mother', which shows רוח הקודש in שלמה's court.

steps.title: רבא: יהודה could have figured it out by counting
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that יהודה did not need a בת קול. He counted the months and days, and they matched.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do you know this? Maybe יהודה counted the months and days, and it matched. What we see, we rely on; what we do not see, we do not rely on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the proof for the court of שם. יהודה could have known on his own that the child was his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהודה knew he had been with תמר, and the timing of her pregnancy fit exactly. We go by what we actually know. A possible other man is something nobody saw, so we do not worry about it. That means there is no need for a בת קול in יהודה's case.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this? It shows the proof is not forced.
We assume, we treat something as established (from חֲזָקָה)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying there was no רוח הקודש at all. He is only saying these פסוקים do not prove it, because there is another way to explain them.

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do you know this?
Maybe Yehuda,
since he calculated the months and days and it matched,
phrases.notes: He means יהודה counted from the time he was with תמר, and the length of her pregnancy fit.

phrases.english: what we see, we rely on;
what we do not see, we do not rely on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the proof for the court of שם and questions it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof of רוח הקודש in the court of שם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: יהודה could know through ordinary reasoning: the timing matched, and an unseen other man is not a real concern. So no בת קול is needed.

steps.title: רבא: 'He said' can mean all of Israel
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that the singular 'he said' can refer to the whole nation, because ישראל is sometimes called by a singular word.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל too: all of ישראל is sometimes spoken of in the singular, as it says: 'ישראל is saved by ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא also pushes back on the proof for the court of שמואל. The singular word does not prove a בת קול spoke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in Step 24 assumed that the people's answer had to be plural. רבא shows that תנ״ך sometimes uses the singular for the whole nation. So 'וַיֹּאמֶר' can simply be the people answering.

keyTerms.meaning: All of ישראל, the whole nation

steps.whyThisMatters: רבא answers both of the questions that led to a בת קול (in יהודה's case and in שמואל's case) with ordinary explanations.

phrases.english: Shmuel too:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלְּהוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל קָרֵי לְהוּ בִּלְשׁוֹן יְחִידִי,
phrases.english: all of Israel is referred to in the singular,
as it is written: "Israel is saved by ה׳."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 45:17

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל נָמֵי כּוּלְּהוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל קָרֵי לְהוּ בִּלְשׁוֹן יְחִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's pushback, now against the proof for the court of שמואל.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof of רוח הקודש in the court of שמואל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The question in Step 24 assumed the people's answer must be plural, but the nation is often called by a singular word, as in ישעיהו 45:17.

steps.title: שלמה could also have figured it out by himself
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that שלמה also did not need a רוח הקודש. He could have seen that one woman was showing mercy and the other was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: שלמה too: he could have known from the fact that this woman was merciful and that woman was not merciful!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the last of the three proofs. He shows that שלמה could have decided the case using simple common sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 28, the answer was that 'she is his mother' came from a בת קול. רבא now says שלמה did not need one. The woman who begged to spare the baby was clearly the real mother, so the פסוק proves nothing about a heavenly voice.

keyTerms.meaning: King Solomon, who judged the case of the two women

phrases.english: Solomon too:
from the fact that this one is merciful
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean the same thing.

phrases.english: and this one is not merciful!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third parallel rejection by רבא, following his rejections about יהודה (step 29) and שמואל (step 30)
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from שלמה's case that a רוח הקודש appeared
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שלמה could have reached his ruling through ordinary reasoning: the merciful woman is the real mother.

steps.title: רבא's conclusion: it is a received tradition
steps.stepSummary: Since none of the פסוקים proves it, רבא concludes that we know about the רוח הקודש in these three places from a tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא wraps up. The idea is true, but the source is a passed-down tradition, not the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not deny that a רוח הקודש appeared in the three places. He only denies that the פסוקים prove it. The teaching stands, but it rests on tradition instead of on the reading of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: here: a received tradition passed down from teacher to student

steps.confusionAlert: Here גמרא does not mean the Talmud. It means a tradition that was handed down.
steps.whatToRemember: The three appearances of רוח הקודש (in the courts of שם, שמואל and שלמה) are known from tradition, not proven from the פסוקים.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a tradition.
phrases.notes: רבא means we know about the רוח הקודש here from what was handed down, not from the פסוקים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רבא's three rejections
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The appearance of a רוח הקודש in these three cases is known through tradition, not from the פסוקים.

steps.title: רבי שמלאי: 613 מצוות were given to משה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי teaches that משה received 613 מצוות. 365 are לאוין, matching the days of the solar year, and 248 are עשה, matching a person's limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמלאי taught: 613 מצוות were said to משה. 365 לאוין match the number of days in the solar year, and 248 מצוות עשה match the limbs of a person.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new teaching begins. רבי שמלאי gives the famous count of 613 מצוות and splits it into two groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 365 לאוין line up with the days of the year, and the 248 עשה line up with the body's limbs. Together they make 613, the total number of מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: the days of the solar year (365)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the count of תרי״ג מצוות, which later הלכה works build on.

phrases.english: Rabbi Simlai taught:
six hundred and thirteen מצוות
were said to Moses,
three hundred and sixty-five prohibitions
like the number of days of the solar year,
and two hundred and forty-eight positive מצוות
corresponding to the limbs of a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after רבא's conclusion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה received 613 מצוות: 365 לאוין and 248 עשה.

steps.title: רב המנונא gives the פסוק that hints to 613
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא asks which פסוק hints to the number 613. He brings 'תורה צוה לנו משה' and begins to work out the גימטריא of the word תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: What is the פסוק? 'משה commanded us the תורה, an inheritance.' The word 'תורה' in גימטריא…
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא brings a פסוק to support רבי שמלאי's number. He starts to show it through the numerical value of a word, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the letters of the word תורה add up to a number connected to the 613 מצוות. The actual calculation comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the verse (that supports this)?
the numerical value of a word's letters

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said: What is the verse?
"Moses commanded us the Torah, an inheritance,"
phrases.notes: דברים 33:4

phrases.english: "Torah" in gimatriya
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, where the גמרא gives the number.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק that hints to רבי שמלאי's count
steps.raayaObject: The number 613 מצוות given to משה
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 33:4, 'תורה צוה לנו משה מורשה', read through גימטריא
